purpose: Decide whether the extra branch/loop code is worth retaining. These are local engineering acceptance thresholds, not confidence intervals or device budgets.
requirements: All original, SDK, installed game, failure and renderer checks pass with unchanged accepted expectations.
Run the unchanged 13-workload/6-memory-case plan twice, comparing native v0.35, the retained reentry candidate and the timer candidate.
Independent-live-timers median is at least 3% below the reentry candidate in each independent run.
No other planned workload has a median regression greater than 5% against the reentry candidate in both independent runs.
Used/active Actor retained-memory medians remain within 16 bytes per actor of the reentry candidate in both runs, with all collection witnesses released.
All existing code-size limits remain unchanged and pass.
failureAction: If the requirements are not met, restore the simpler reentry implementation while retaining the new behavior tests, the candidate and all measurements. Do not repeat trials merely to seek a passing ranking.
limits: Passing permits retaining this implementation; it establishes neither statistical certainty nor a whole-game, native-engine, Steam Deck or mobile performance claim. Grant costs remain a separate documented boundary cost.
